common_name: Pia Dwarf Hydrangea (Compact German Rose-Pink Mophead)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in rich, moist, well-drained soil in partial shade.

directions: Pia is a true dwarf mophead hydrangea, staying under two feet tall and wide, which makes it one of the few old-fashioned bigleaf cultivars suited to containers, rock garden edges, and tight foundation plantings. Its compact flower heads run rose-pink in neutral to alkaline soil and shift toward violet-blue with added soil acidity, following the same aluminum-uptake pattern as full-size mopheads. Because its small root mass dries out faster than larger cultivars, keep soil consistently moist and mulched through summer heat. Prune only immediately after flowering, since blooms form on the previous season's wood.

common_name: Gertrud Glahn Hydrangea (Antique German Semi-Double Mophead)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in rich, moist, well-drained soil in partial shade with protection from hot afternoon sun.

directions: Gertrud Glahn is an older German mophead selection whose florets carry an extra, slightly ruffled petal layer, giving the flower heads a fuller, semi-double texture than typical single-ray mopheads. Color runs pink in neutral-to-alkaline soil and deepens toward blue-purple as soil acidity increases, with the semi-double form holding its shape well even after summer rain. Grow it in humus-rich, evenly moist soil in dappled or afternoon shade, mulching to protect roots from heat stress. As an old-wood bloomer, prune only right after flowering to avoid cutting off next year's buds.

directions: Alpengluhen (sometimes sold as 'Alpenglow') is a vigorous German-bred mophead valued for unusually saturated, deep carmine-red to burgundy flower heads that stay intense even without heavy soil acidification. In more acidic soil the red takes on purple tones rather than shifting fully blue, giving it a distinct look among classic old-wood bloomers. Plant in rich, consistently moist soil with dappled or afternoon shade, and mulch to keep roots cool through summer heat. Prune only immediately after flowering, since it blooms on the prior season's wood.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in rich, moist, well-drained soil in partial shade.

directions: Europa is an old, large-growing mophead hydrangea noted for unusually big, dense flower heads carried on sturdy, upright stems that resist flopping under their own weight. Color runs deep pink in neutral-to-alkaline soil and shifts toward violet-blue with added soil acidity, in keeping with its classic old-wood-blooming habit. Give it a generous planting area with rich, evenly moist soil and afternoon shade, since its larger leaves and flower heads lose moisture quickly in summer heat. Prune only right after flowering to preserve the buds that will form next year's blooms.
